questions.q: You run mvn package. Which phases does Maven execute?
o: Every phase of the default lifecycle up to and including package
Only the package phase and nothing before it
Every phase up to package, then install and deploy as well
Only the phases whose plugins changed since the last build
questions.w: Asking for a phase runs all earlier phases in order: compile, test, then package. install and deploy come after package and are not run.

questions.q: What is the difference between a Maven phase and a goal?
o: A goal is a plugin task, and goals are bound to phases to do the work
A phase is a plugin task, and goals are the stages of the lifecycle
Phases run in parallel, whereas goals always run one after another
A goal is a phase that has been renamed in the parent pom
questions.w: Phases are named steps with no behaviour. Plugin goals such as compiler:compile are attached to them, and a goal can also be run directly.

questions.q: Two libraries need different versions of Jackson. Which version does Maven use by default?
o: The one nearest to your project in the dependency tree
The highest version number found anywhere in the tree
The lowest version number found anywhere in the tree
Neither, and the build fails with a version conflict
questions.w: Maven uses nearest definition, and the first declared on a tie. It is not the newest, so an older version can win. Manage the version to be sure.

o: Sets the version and scope to use when an artifact is needed, adding nothing itself
Adds every listed library to the classpath of the project
Removes the transitive dependencies of the listed libraries
Downloads the listed libraries ahead of the next build
questions.w: It only declares versions. A dependency still has to be listed in dependencies, but it can then omit the version. A BOM is a pom made of this section.

questions.q: Which scope suits a JDBC driver that the code never compiles against?
o: runtime, because it is needed to run but not to compile
provided, because the application server always supplies it
test, because only the integration tests connect to it
compile, because every library must be on the compile classpath
questions.w: runtime puts the driver on the runtime and test classpaths but not the compile classpath, and it is packaged with the application.

questions.q: In a multi-module build, what decides the order in which modules are built?
o: The dependencies between the modules, worked out by the reactor
The order the modules are listed in the parent pom
The alphabetical order of the module directory names
The size of each module, with the smallest built first
questions.w: The reactor sorts modules by their inter-module dependencies, whatever the list order. Circular dependencies cause an error.

questions.q: What does mvn install do that mvn package does not?
o: Copies the artifact into the local repository in ~/.m2
Uploads the artifact to the company Nexus server
Runs the integration tests that package skips
Deletes the target directory before it builds
questions.w: install is the phase after verify. It copies the jar into ~/.m2 so other local projects can use it. Uploading to a remote repository is deploy.

questions.q: Why would you use the Maven Wrapper (mvnw)?
o: Everyone and the CI server run the same Maven version without installing it
It makes the compiler faster by keeping the JVM running between builds
It lets a project be built without a pom.xml file
It replaces the local repository with a shared cache
questions.w: The wrapper downloads the Maven version recorded in .mvn/wrapper, which removes differences between machines.
